text.p: Malaysian construction and property group Transwater Corp Bhd has made a privatisation proposal to replace the existing causeway linking Malaysia and Singapore with a road and rail bridge.
The project would include development of the waterfront area at the proposed gateway and rebuilding of the customs and immigration complex, it said in a statement on Wednesday.
The proposed build, operate and transfer project, to be developed over a period of 30 years, would cost about 1.1 billion ringgit, it said.

Transwater said it had also submitted another proposal to the government to redevelop a 23.9-acre piece of land in Kuala Lumpur. The land would be developed into a mixed development consisting office blocks, service apartments and a shopping complex, it said.

The company also plans to acquire a further 1,563 acres of land from a subsidiary of Berjaya Group Bhd for 156.3 million ringgit. It had earlier proposed to buy 3,875.7 acres of land from the Berjaya Group unit, also at 100,000 ringgit per acre.
